content:
Hi everyone! I recently made a short guide (4 pages) on the theory behind Lean 4, specifically the Curry-Howard correspondence. I have noticed that a lot of beginners want to understand why mathematical proofs can be verified by a computer, so I designed this guide to answer that question. It is available here: https://zenodo.org/records/23073218

I would love to get feedback on the guide from this community. If people find it useful, I plan on opening a PR to data/documentation.yaml. Thanks for your help!
Can you comment on the AI/LLM use concerning this manuscript?

Absolutely. AI was not used to write any part of the manuscript, it was used to improve the Latex formatting and improve grammar/sentence flow. Additionally, I used it to find extra sources if I needed to develop my understanding.
Just to clarify, “improving grammar and sentence flow” means minor edits to my content, not complete rewrites.
I have opened PR 923 to add this guide under documentation.yaml: https://github.com/leanprover-community/leanprover-community.github.io/pull/923

There's heavy overlap there with existing documentation. For example, Type Theory in Lean already undoubtedly mentions the Curry-Howard correspondence and is at a level more or less similar to what it seems your document explains at.

I don't think I understand what the architecture analogy is clarifying here personally, if a type is a 3x4 block and a constructor is a mold for making one, what's a term? And srely Nat.zero and Nat.succ feel like quite different feeling objects if we architecturepomorphize them.

The bar for adding things there in the docs I suspect is quite high unless you're covering new ground -- perhaps try polishing what you have into a blog post and see if you get good response from readers?
